The first of the New York State Comptroller’s audits of Albany’s waste to energy plants will be released next week, and officials with the state’s Office of Management and Budget (OMB) are urging the comptroller to keep all audit reports confidential. 
  
 At issue with the state’s plants is the way some of the waste is burned. The Office of Energy Efficiency and Conservation (EEC) had found that the plants’ steam turbines were not operating at maximum efficiency, which meant that some of the heat generated from the plant’s furnaces was being lost. The plants’ boilers themselves are also underutilized, according to the audit. 
  
 But the EEC’s report was not the subject of an audit because EEC did not have the authority to review plant operations. A 1974 law stipulated that the Energy and Finance departments had oversight over the state’s waste-to-energy plants.
